attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b), adding two interfaces (opt1=vtnet1=10.50.1.1/24, opt2=vtnet2=10.50.2.1/24) and exactly one firewall pass rule: TCP/8080 from opt1(lan-a) network to opt2(lan-b) network. All other opt1<->opt2 traffic remains blocked by the existing default-deny ruleset. Static addressing (10.50.1.10/24 and 10.50.2.10/24 respectively, with cross routes via node1) was persisted on node2/node3 via NetworkManager, and node3's firewalld was opened for 8080 to allow the test listener. Verified end-to-end before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes: TCP 8080 (node2->node3) succeeds, ICMP and other ports between the two networks are refused, and the reverse direction (node3->node2) is fully refused. Each node's boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) was captured before and after its reboot and confirmed changed, with functional recovery re-verified after each restart.
